# awscc_securityagent_private_connection (Resource)

Resource Type definition for AWS::SecurityAgent::PrivateConnection. A private connection allows Security Agent to reach a target resource privately via a VPC Lattice resource gateway.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `private_connection_name` (String) A unique name for the private connection within your account.

### Optional

- `certificate` (String) The PEM-encoded certificate chain for the private connection.
- `mode` (Attributes) The configuration for the private connection. Specify either a service-managed or a self-managed mode. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mode))
- `tags` (Attributes Set) The tags attached to the private connection. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--tags))

### Read-Only

- `arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the private connection.
- `certificate_expiry_time` (String) The date and time the connection's certificate expires, in UTC format.
- `dns_resolution` (String) The DNS resolution mode for the resource gateway.
- `host_address` (String) The IP address or DNS name of the target resource.
- `id` (String) Uniquely identifies the resource.
- `resource_configuration_id` (String) The identifier or ARN of the VPC Lattice resource configuration.
- `resource_gateway_id` (String) The identifier or ARN of the VPC Lattice resource gateway.
- `status` (String) The current status of the private connection.
- `type` (String) The type of the private connection, indicating whether it is service-managed or self-managed.
- `vpc_id` (String) The identifier of the VPC the resource gateway is created in.

<a id="nestedatt--mode"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mode`

Optional:

- `self_managed` (Attributes) The configuration for a self-managed private connection, where you manage your own resource configuration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mode--self_managed))
- `service_managed` (Attributes) The configuration for a service-managed private connection, where the service manages the resource gateway lifecycle. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--mode--service_managed))

<a id="nestedatt--mode--self_managed"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mode.self_managed`

Optional:

- `resource_configuration_id` (String) The identifier or ARN of the resource configuration.


<a id="nestedatt--mode--service_managed"></a>
### Nested Schema for `mode.service_managed`

Optional:

- `dns_resolution` (String) The DNS resolution mode for the resource gateway.
- `host_address` (String) The IP address or DNS name of the target resource.
- `ip_address_type` (String) The IP address type of the service-managed resource gateway.
- `ipv_4_addresses_per_eni` (Number) The number of IPv4 addresses in each elastic network interface for the service-managed resource gateway.
- `port_ranges` (List of String) The TCP port ranges that a consumer can use to access the resource.
- `security_group_ids` (List of String) The security groups to attach to the service-managed resource gateway.
- `subnet_ids` (List of String) The subnets that the service-managed resource gateway spans.
- `vpc_id` (String) The VPC to create the service-managed resource gateway in.



<a id="nestedatt--tags"></a>
### Nested Schema for `tags`

Optional:

- `key` (String) The key name of the tag.
- `value` (String) The value for the tag.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_securityagent_private_connection.example
  identity = {
    arn = "arn"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `arn` (String) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the private connection

#### Optional

- `account_id` (String) AWS Account where this resource is managed
- `region` (String) Region where this resource is managed

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = awscc_securityagent_private_connection.example
  id = "arn"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

